errors.english: With regard to the nature of the property-possessor and its connection
errors.why: Parallel to the preceding 'contradiction with the nature of the property', this is the fallacy of a thesis contradicting the nature of the property-possessor (dharmisvarūpaviruddha); 'and its connection' misreads the heading.

errors.english: "The object-possessors of the uncompounded are useful for others"
errors.why: The example says 'these [eyes etc.] serve the purpose of another, an uncompounded subject (viṣayin)', not that object-possessors of the uncompounded serve others.

errors.english: The meaning of the word "oneself" is "nature."
errors.why: bdag nyid here glosses svayam as 'oneself' (ātman, i.e. the proponent himself), not 'nature'.

note: Generally follows the commentary on svayam iṣṭaḥ, with a few slips in the examples of thesis fallacies and one gloss.

errors.why: The referent is the one Tathāgata, the Buddha, honouring his father Śuddhodana's body; the plural with the note 'the Buddhas' misidentifies who acts.

note: Faithful rendering of the Avadānakalpalatā verses; only the plural Tathāgatas misleads.
Accurate rendering of the Vinaya commentary on the five kinds of seed, bhūtagrāma and the pāyantika definition.

errors.english: The text states that the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin) the whole composed of parts produces the cognition.
errors.why: The objector says recognition and the parts produce the cognition OF the whole; the whole is the object of the cognition, not its producer.

fix.find: The text states that the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin) the whole composed of parts produces the cognition.
fix.replace: That is, recognition and the parts produce the cognition of the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin), the whole composed of parts.

errors.why: This completes 'nus pa tha dad par gyur ba' from the previous side: there is no coming-to-be of a distinct capacity; gyur ba is not 'transformation' here.

errors.english: is a sign established by direct perception
errors.why: The sign is one whose relation (sambandha) is established by perception; 'relation' is dropped, changing the point about how the inference works.

note: The Nyāya avayavin debate is broadly followed, but the objector's claim about what produces the cognition of the whole is inverted.

errors.english: introduces the Sāṃkhya [note: original: གྲངས་ཅན་, a school of Hindu philosophy] position
errors.why: Glossed as 'namely colour etc.', this says the 'etc.' sets out the enumerated items (colour and the rest), not a Sāṃkhya position.

errors.english: [note: original: རྗེས་སུ་འགྲོ་བ་, Sanskrit: anvaya; the presence of a property in similar cases]
errors.why: Here rjes su 'gro ba is the universal's recurrence through its individuals (anugama), not anvaya as positive concomitance with similar cases.

errors.english: It refers to seeing however many things there are that are being excluded [note: original: བསལ་བ་, Sanskrit: apoha; the theory that words function by excluding what they are not]
errors.why: Glossing 'how many individuals', bsal ba stands for gsal ba (individual, vyakti): seeing as many individuals as there are; apoha is not in question.

note: The thread of the argument on universals is mostly kept, but several glosses import the wrong technical frame.

errors.english: is considered to be included in trees that have blooming flowers, then it is reasonable to call this inclusion "meeting in one object."
errors.why: 'du ba is the Vaiśeṣika category of inherence (samavāya): the number 'many' inheres in the trees, which is called inherence in a single object.

fix.find: is considered to be included in trees that have blooming flowers, then it is reasonable to call this inclusion "meeting in one object."
fix.replace: inheres in trees that have blooming flowers, then it is reasonable to call this "inherence in a single object."

errors.english: "variegated" does not include the limbs that are present here
errors.why: yan lag can is the whole (avayavin), not the limbs: variegatedness does not inhere in the whole in which conjunction is present; the following verse line 'because each is not variegated' is the root text supporting this.

fix.find: "variegated" does not include the limbs that are present here
fix.replace: variegatedness does not inhere in the whole (avayavin) in which conjunction is present here

errors.english: If a forest of a multitude of numbers
errors.why: The side opens with the verdict 'these two are not alike' (the forest example and variegatedness), which is not translated.

errors.english: Therefore one object has many objects.
errors.why: The verse says one [cognition] has many objects.

note: The later argument on superimposition is serviceable, but the opening on inherence and the whole misrenders the key Vaiśeṣika terms.

span_why: The opening ('The husband replied, "Good lady, what you say is not wrong..." ... "Dear girl, be joyful..."') translates the previous side's last line.

errors.why: With 'bu mo dga'' from the previous side this is 'dga' zhing las byos shig', 'do your work gladly'; there are no fields.

note: The Upananda narrative is rendered faithfully apart from the misparsed command and the material carried over from the previous side.
A sound rendering of the body-consciousness argument; some phrasing (the milk example) is loose but not wrong enough to correct with confidence.

errors.english: If the support causes the destruction of staying by itself or through another
errors.why: The Tibetan says the support makes the perishing thing stay, not that it destroys staying.

note: The refutation of the support is followable, but a technical term and the role of the support are misrendered.
